nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ لاَ عَاصِمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: that it is an exception (istithnāʾ) not of the same kind as what precedes it.
The other: that it is by way of attribution (nisba), so that the meaning is "there is no one protected (maʿṣūm)", as He said ﴿مِنْ مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ﴾, i.e. poured out (madfūq).
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr mentioned a third view and claimed it is the most fitting of what has been said about it. He said: There is no one to withhold today from the command of Allah — which has come down upon the creation in the form of drowning and destruction — ﴿إلاَّ مَنْ رَحِمَ﴾, i.e. except Allah, just as you say: "There is no rescuer today except Allah." So مَنْ is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ), and you do not make "عاصم" mean معصوم (protected), nor "إلاَّ" mean "لكنْ" (but).
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُغْرَقِينَ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, the water came between the son of Noah and the mountain, so he was among the drowned.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقِيلَ يٰأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِي مَآءَكِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, swallow all the water that is upon you. ﴿وَيٰسَمَآءُ أَقْلِعِي﴾, i.e. do not rain.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَغِيضَ ٱلْمَآءُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, it decreased.
Qatāda said: That is, it went away.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾, i.e. the matter of their destruction was decreed.
Then He said: ﴿وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِيِّ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is the mountain of Mosul.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَالِحٍ﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
Among them: that the meaning is that he is one possessed of deeds that are not righteous.
It is also said: His deed is a deed that is not righteous.
Qatāda said: Its meaning is: your asking Me about that of which you have no knowledge — in his saying ﴿سَآوِي إلَى جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ المَاءِ﴾ — is a deed that is not righteous, and this is a deed that is not righteous.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the best of what has been said about it, because ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read ﴿إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غيرُ صَالحٍ أن تسألني ما ليس لك به عِلمٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قِيلَ يٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلاَمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَركَاتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: Every believer until the Day of Resurrection is included in this, and every wicked person until the Day of Resurrection is included in His saying ﴿وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said something similar to this, except that it was in different wording. Its implied form (taqdīr) in Arabic according to his view is: "upon the offspring of nations from among those with you, and the offspring of nations whom We will grant enjoyment"; then [the word "offspring"] was omitted, as He said ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَريَةَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهَآ إِلَيْكَ مَا كُنتَ تَعْلَمُهَآ أَنتَ وَلاَ قَوْمُكَ مِن قَبْلِ هَـٰذَا﴾.
That is: what We have revealed to you of the account of Noah, you did not know it, neither you nor your people, because they were not people of a scripture.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰقَوْمِ لاۤ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلاَّ عَلَى ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِيۤ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, [the One who] created me.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيٰقَوْمِ ٱسْتَغْفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوۤاْ إِلَيْهِ يُرْسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّدْرَاراً﴾.
It is narrated that they were people of crops and cultivation, and they used to live in sand tracts between Syria and Yemen. Then He sent the wind against them, and it would enter their noses and come out of their rear ends and tear them apart.
And ﴿مِدْرَاراً﴾ is for intensification: that is, [rain] following one upon another.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَزِدْكُمْ قُوَّةً إِلَىٰ قُوَّتِكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, strength added to your strength.
Someone else said: They had gone three years without children being born to them.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن نَّقُولُ إِلاَّ ٱعْتَرَاكَ بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنَا بِسُوۤءٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: [One of our gods] has afflicted you with evil, i.e. with madness, because of your reviling them.
It is said: عَراه, اعتراه and اعترَّه, when something befalls him; and from it is ﴿وَأَطْعِمُوا القَانِعَ وَالمُعْتَرَّ﴾. The poet said:
أتَيْتُكَ عَارِياً خَلَقاً ثِيَابِي * عَلَى خَوْفٍ تُظَنُّ بِيَ الظُّنُونُ
(I came to you bare, my clothes worn out, in fear, with suspicions being held about me.)
The meaning: We say nothing except that one of our gods has afflicted you with madness, because of your reviling them.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنِّيۤ أُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ وَٱشْهَدُوۤاْ أَنِّي بَرِيۤءٌ مِّمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ، مِن دُونِهِ فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعاً ثُمَّ لاَ تُنظِرُونِ﴾.
This is among the signs of prophethood: that the messenger, being alone, says to his people "فَكِيدوني جَمِيعاً" (so plot against me all together). Likewise the Prophet ﷺ said [this] to Quraysh, and Noah ﷺ said ﴿فأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَاءكُمْ ثُمَّ لاَ يَكُنْ أمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً﴾.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنِّي تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلاَّ هُوَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ﴾.
That is, it is in His grasp, and His power reaches it.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, upon the truth; i.e. He recompenses the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil, wrongs no one, and accepts nothing but faith in Him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-ṣirāṭ in the language is the clear path.
The meaning: Allah, exalted be His praise, even though He has power over everything, does not seize them except with justice (bi-l-ḥaqq).

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَضُرُّونَهُ شَيْئاً﴾.
That is, you are not able to harm Him in any way if He wills to destroy you.
It is also said: Your destruction does not harm Him if He destroys you, i.e. you do not diminish Him in anything, because it is the same to Him whether you exist or do not exist.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ﴾.
That is, He protects me from [your] reaching me with harm.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّبَعُوۤاْ أَمْرَ كُلِّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾.
Al-ʿanīd, al-ʿanūd and al-ʿānid: one who resists [the truth] without right.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأُتْبِعُواْ فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا لَعْنَةً﴾.
That is, and they were made to be pursued [by it].
And the meaning of ﴿فَمَا تَزِيدُونَنِي غَيْرَ تَخْسِيرٍ﴾ is: nothing but loss for you, if you increase in disbelief.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيٰقَوْمِ هَـٰذِهِ نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً﴾.
It is narrated that she came out of a rock.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابٌ قَرِيبٌ﴾.
That is, near to whoever touches her [with harm].

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَصْبَحُواْ فِي دِيَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, dead.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْاْ فِيهَآ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, as though they had never lived there.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: Al-maghānī are dwelling places.
Someone else said: غَنِيتُ بالمكان means "I stayed in the place."
The meaning: as though they had never resided there in joy and well-being.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بِٱلْبُـشْرَىٰ﴾.
That is, with the glad tidings of a child.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ سَلاَماً قَالَ سَلاَمٌ﴾ [verse 69].
And it is read ﴿قَال سِلْمٌ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: سِلْمٌ and سَلاَمٌ are the same, just as one says حِلٌّ and حَلاَلٌ.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ﴾.
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: It is the well-cooked; and Qatāda said the same.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is that over which fire is kindled until it is cooked.
And the saying of Abū ʿUbayda: ﴿حَنِيذٍ﴾ has the meaning of maḥnūdh, i.e. roasted; one says حَنَذْتُ فرسي, i.e. I made my horse sweat. [Translator's note: the source has «وقول أبو عبيدة», with أبو in the nominative after a muḍāf; translated as written.]
The meaning: he did not delay, when they came to him as guests, in bringing them a calf; then the bāʾ was omitted from "أنْ" [i.e. بأن جاء].
It is said: The messengers were Gabriel, Michael and Isrāfīl, peace be upon them; ﴿بِٱلْبُـشْرَىٰ﴾: the glad tidings of Isaac.
It is also said: the glad tidings of the destruction of the people of Lot.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَى أَيْدِيَهُمْ لاَ تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ﴾.
One says نَكِرَ, أَنْكَرَ and استنكر with the same meaning.
Qatāda said: When a guest arrived and did not eat, they would consider that he had not come with good, and that he had come with evil.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً﴾.
That is, he harboured [fear] inwardly.
﴿قَالُواْ لاَ تَخَفْ إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنَا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ﴾, i.e. we have been sent with the punishment. ﴿وَامْرَأَتُهُ قَائِمَةٌ﴾, while he was sitting.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْنَاهَا بِإِسْحَاقَ وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾.
There are several views on it:
The best of them: that when they did not eat, he found them strange and feared them; then when they said "Do not fear" and informed him that they were messengers, he rejoiced at that, and his wife laughed out of joy at his rejoicing.
Al-Farrāʾ reported that one of the exegetes said: The meaning is: "So We gave her glad tidings of Isaac, and she laughed."
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is not sound, because placing before and after (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr) does not occur with the fāʾ.
It is also said: "she laughed", i.e. she menstruated.
This is a view that is not known and is not sound.
It is also said: She had said to him: "I reckon that a punishment will descend upon these people, so take Lot to yourself." Then when the messengers came with what she had said, she was delighted by it and laughed. This, if its chain of transmission is sound, is good.
Qatāda said: She laughed at the heedlessness of the people when the punishment had come to them.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: Al-warāʾ is the child's child.
One of the people of reasoning said: In this there is evidence that Ishmael is the one who was to be sacrificed, because she was given the glad tidings that she would live until Isaac was born, and until Jacob was born to Isaac; so how could he be commanded to sacrifice him when she had been given the glad tidings that [a child] would be born to him?

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَتْ يَٰوَيْلَتَىٰ أَأَلِدُ وَأَنَاْ عَجُوزٌ وَهَـٰذَا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is narrated that when she was given the glad tidings she was ninety-eight years old, and Abraham was one year older than her.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلرَّوْعُ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, the fright.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَآءَتْهُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ﴾.
Qatāda said: They gave him the glad tidings that they had come only with the punishment for the people of Lot, and that he need not fear.
Maʿmar said: Someone other than Qatāda said: They gave him the glad tidings of Isaac.
Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl narrated from Jundab from Ḥudhayfa, who said: The disputing here is that he said to them: "Do you think, if there were fifty Muslims among them, would you destroy them?" They said: "No." He said: "Then if there were forty among them?" They said: "No." He said: "Then if there were thirty among them?" They said: "No." He said: "Then if there were twenty among them?" They said: "No." He said: "Then if there were ten, or five among them?" — Ḥumayd was unsure — they said: "No." Qatāda said something similar, and said: Then he — meaning Abraham — said: "A people among whom there are not ten Muslims, there is no good in them." ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura said: They were four hundred thousand.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطاً سِيۤءَ بِهِمْ﴾.
That is: their coming grieved him, because of what he knew of his people.
It is narrated that they came to him and asked to be his guests, so he stood up with them. They had been commanded not to destroy them until Lot had borne witness against them three times; so he said to them: "My people are the worst of Allah's creation," three times.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعاً﴾.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: One says "ضقت بالأمر ذرعاً" (I was straitened in arm by the matter) when you do not find it within your capacity to carry it out. It is taken from al-dhirāʿ (the forearm), because strength lies in it.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, severe. And that is known in the language; one says — and that is known in the language; one says — عَصِيبٌ and عَصَبْصَبٌ for what is severe and grim. [Translator's note: the phrase «وذلك يُعرفُ في اللغة، يقال» is repeated in the source; translated as written.]

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَآءَهُ قَوْمُهُ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, they hasten.
Mujāhid said: They trot in their walking.
The lexicographers said: One says أُهْرِعَ when someone comes hurrying, and is trembling at the same time.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ يٰقَوْمِ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ بَنَاتِي هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ﴾.
There are several views on it:
The best of them is the view of Mujāhid, who said: He means the women of his community. This is strengthened by the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وأزواجُهُ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ﴾.
And it is narrated that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Masʿūd read ﴿وأزواجهُ أمَّهَاتُهُم وَهو أبٌ لهم﴾.
It is also said: The meaning is: "These are my daughters, if you accept Islam."
It is also said: In their religion it was permissible for a disbeliever to marry a Muslim woman.
ʿIkrima said: He did not offer them his daughters, nor the daughters of his community; he only said this to them so that they would go away.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ آوِيۤ إِلَىٰ رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the clan.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, in a portion of the night. One says سَرَى and أسْرَى when someone travels by night.
If it is said: Al-surā (night travel) is only by night, so what is the meaning of "in a portion of the night"?
The answer: had He not said ﴿بِقِطْعٍ مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾, it could have been at its beginning.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ ٱمْرَأَتَكَ﴾.
The meaning: so travel by night with your family, except your wife.
And it is narrated that it is like this in one of the readings; and Abū ʿAmr read ﴿إلاَّ امرأتُكَ﴾ in the nominative.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةً مِّن سِجِّيلٍ﴾.
There are several views on it:
Mujāhid said: It is Persian, i.e. its first part is "stone" and its last part is "clay".
Qatāda said: That is, of clay.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These two views are good.
Mujāhid held only that its origin is Persian and that it was then Arabicised.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We considered it good only because He said in another place ﴿حِجَارةً من طِينٍ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: Al-sijjīl is the severe, and he recited:
* "ضَرْباً تَوَاصَى بهِ الأبْطَالُ سِجَّيناً" *
(A striking that the champions enjoined on one another, severe.)
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim rejected this view of his and said: This is sijjīn and that is sijjīl, so how can it be cited as evidence?
Abū Jaʿfar said: This rejection is not binding, because Abū ʿUbayda held that the lām is a substitute for the nūn, because of the closeness of one of them to the other.
But Abū ʿUbayda's view is rejected from another angle: namely that, were it as he said, it would be "حجارةً سِجِّيلاً" (severe stones), because one does not say "stones of severe", since "severe" is a naʿt (adjective).
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَّنْضُودٍ﴾, i.e. one part of it lying upon another. One says نَضَدْتُ المَتَاعَ واللَّبِنَ (I stacked the goods and the bricks) when you put one part of it upon another, so it is manḍūd and naḍīd. The poet said:
خَلَّتْ سَبِيلَ أَتِيٍّ كَانَ يَحْبِسُهُ * ورفَّعتهُ إلَى السِّجفَيْنِ فَالنَّضَدِ
(She cleared the way of a stream that was holding it back, and raised it up to the two curtains and then to the stacked goods.)
It is also said: Sijjīl is from their saying أسْجَلْتُ, when you give. And it is said: It is from al-sijill (the written record), as though it were among what was written against them and decreed to befall them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq considers this view good. He said: It is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنَّ كِتَابَ الفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ. وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سِجِّين. كِتَابٌ مَرْقُومٌ﴾, and sijjīn and sijjīl are the same.

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَآءِ ٱلْقُرَىٰ نَقُصُّهُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْهَا قَآئِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: The standing is what has fallen in upon its roofs, and the mown-down is what has no trace left.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا زَادُوهُمْ غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: nothing but loss.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And so it is according to the lexicographers; and from it is ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدَا أبِي لَهَبٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لاَ تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.
And He has said in another place: ﴿وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ يَتَسَاءلُونَ﴾.
There are two answers to this:
One of them: that it is like His saying ﴿هَذَا يَوْمُ لاَ يَنْطِقُونَ﴾.
And the meaning is: they do not utter any argument in their favour; just as it is said of someone who talks a great deal without a clear argument: "He brought nothing, and said nothing."
The other answer: that on that Day there are terrors and hardships; at one time they are prevented from speaking, and at another time they are given permission. On this view: ﴿لاَ تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, who said: "When ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ﴾ was revealed, I said: O Messenger of Allah, then on what basis do we act — on something already settled, or on something not yet settled? He said: Rather, on something already settled, O ʿUmar, with which the pens have run; but each is eased towards that for which he was created."

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ شَقُواْ فَفِي ٱلنَّارِ لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ. خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ وَٱلأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ﴾.
There are several answers on this. Among them: that the Arabs were addressed according to what they know and use, and they say: "I will not speak to you as long as night and day alternate, and as long as the heavens and the earth endure," meaning by that: forever.
And the meaning of ﴿إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ﴾ would be: besides what your Lord wills, of increase for the people of the Fire in punishment and for the people of Paradise in bliss; and it is authentically established that they will be given increase.
Al-Aʿmash narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to the heart of a human being — leave aside what you have been made aware of." Then Abū Hurayra recited ﴿فَلاَ تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ﴾.
It is also said: The meaning of (إلاَّ) is also the meaning of "سوى" (besides), except that the meaning is: besides what your Lord wills of increase in the eternal abiding.
These are two good views, because it is well known in the language to say: "You are owed such-and-such by me, except (illā) such-and-such," and "besides (siwā) such-and-such," and "other than (ghayra) such-and-such."
Sībawayh reported: "لو كان معي رجل إلا زيدٌ" (if there were with me a man other than Zayd); this has the meaning of siwā and ghayr.
And the Kufans reported: "لك عندي ألفٌ إلاَّ ألفين" (you are owed a thousand by me besides the two thousand); and "إلاَّ" in the like of this is explained as meaning "سوى, غير, لكن" (besides, other than, but), and the meanings are close to one another.
It is also said: This is an exception because they remain in their graves; so the meaning on this view is ﴿إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ﴾ of their stay in their graves.
It is also said: This is an exception because some people from among the monotheists enter the Fire and then come out of it.
So the meaning on this view: abiding eternally in the Fire ﴿مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ وَٱلأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ﴾ of bringing out whomever He wills by His mercy and by the intercession of the Prophet ﷺ.
Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَسَى أنْ يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَاماً مَحْمُوداً﴾: It is the intercession.
And the meaning regarding the people of Paradise would be: abiding eternally in it as long as the heavens and the earth endure ﴿إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ﴾ of some people's entering the Fire and their coming out to Paradise.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Azdī narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd ibn Mūsā al-Baṣrī, known as al-Makkī, narrated to us: Shaybān ibn Farrūkh narrated to us: Abū Hilāl narrated to us: Qatāda narrated to us concerning this verse ﴿وَأمَّا الَّذِينَ شَقُوا فَفِي النَّارِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ﴾, and at this point he said: Anas ibn Mālik narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A people will come out of the Fire." Qatāda said: We do not say as the people of Ḥarūrāʾ say. [Translator's note: the source has «غلى قوله», evidently a misprint for «إلى قوله» (up to His saying); translated accordingly.]
It is also said: There is a fifth view on this, namely that the meaning is: abiding in it forever; then He said ﴿إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ﴾, addressing them according to what they know of [the formula of] exception, and referring the matter back to Allah, exalted be His majesty, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿لَتَدْخُلَنَّ المَسْجِدَ الحَرَامَ إنْ شَاءَ اللهُ آمِنِينَ﴾. And He has made this clear by His saying ﴿عَطَاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ﴾; Mujāhid said: That is, not cut off.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is well known in the language; one says جَذَذْتُ الشَّيءَ, i.e. I cut it.
A sixth view has been stated on this verse: the exception is for their standing in the open plain (ʿarṣa) of the Resurrection.
Qatāda said: This heaven and this earth will be replaced.
So the meaning: abiding in it as long as that heaven and that earth, which replace these two, endure. [Translator's note: the source has «تلمك», evidently a misprint for «تلك» (that); translated accordingly.]

nahhas-meani:109-109.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَمُوَفُّوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ غَيْرَ مَنقُوصٍ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Jābir, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: [That is,] what has been written for them of good or evil.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ﴾.
That is, of postponement until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, meaning in this world.

nahhas-meani:113-113.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَلاَ تَرْكَنُوۤاْ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ فَتَمَسَّكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ﴾.
ʿIkrima said: That is, [do not] show them affection and obey them.

nahhas-meani:114-114.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلاَةَ طَرَفَيِ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَزُلَفاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: The two ends of the day are the dawn (ṣubḥ) and the afternoon (ʿaṣr) [prayers]; ﴿وَزُلَفاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ is the sunset (maghrib) and the night (ʿishāʾ) [prayers]. The Prophet ﷺ said: "They are the two zulfas of the night."
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, who said: The two ends of the day are the dawn, and the noon (ẓuhr) and the afternoon; ﴿وَزُلَفاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ is the ʿishāʾ and the ʿatama.
Ḥajjāj narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid: ﴿وَزُلَفاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾: he said: an hour of the night, up to the ʿatama.
Mujāhid's first view is better, because by it the five prayers are brought together.
And because Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿نَّ ٱلْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ ٱلسَّـيِّئَاتِ﴾: He means the five prayers. [Translator's note: the quotation is printed in the source without the initial hamza of «إِنَّ».]
ʿAlqama and al-Aswad narrated from ʿAbd Allāh that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I found a woman in a garden, and I kissed her and embraced her, and I had everything of her except intercourse; so do with me what you will." Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed ﴿وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلاَةَ طَرَفَيِ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَزُلَفاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ إِنَّ ٱلْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ ٱلسَّـيِّئَاتِ﴾. Muʿādh ibn Jabal said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it particular to him, or general for people?" He said: "Rather, general."
The known reading of Mujāhid is "وزُلْفَى", with ḍamma on the zāy and with the letter of the feminine.
Ibn Muḥayṣin read with this reading, except that he added nunation in continuous recitation. It is also read ﴿وَزُلُفاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾, which is a singular like al-ḥulum. The well-known reading is ﴿وزُلَفاً﴾. And Sībawayh recited:
طيَّ اللَّيالِي زُلَفاً فَزُلَفَا * سَمَاوَةَ الهِلاَلِ حَتَّى احْقَوْقَفَا
(As the nights fold, hour upon hour, the outline of the new moon, until it became bent.)
It is the plural of zulfa, which is an hour drawing near to another; and from it comes al-zalfa (nearness), and from it al-Muzdalifa was named, because it is a halting place that draws near to ʿArafa.

nahhas-meani:116-116.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ أُوْلُواْ بَقِيَّةٍ﴾.
It is said: people of obedience.
It is also said: people of discernment.
It is also said: people with a share from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مَآ أُتْرِفُواْ فِيهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: [That is,] of their dominion, their tyranny, and their abandoning the truth.

nahhas-meani:118-118.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾.
That is, upon a single religion.

nahhas-meani:119-119.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ، إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ رَبُّكَ وَلِذٰلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This verse is among the difficult ones, and several views have been stated about it.
ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī narrated from Mujāhid that he said: And for mercy He created them.
And Qatāda said the same.
Several views on it are narrated from al-Ḥasan:
Among them, that he said: And for disagreement He created them.
Among them: that it is said: And for mercy He created them.
And among them, that he said: He created them for Paradise and the Fire, for wretchedness and felicity.
It is said: This is the view held by the people of the Sunna, and it is the clearest and most comprehensive of them.
What ʿAbd al-Karīm narrated from Mujāhid does not contradict it, because Ḥajjāj has clarified it in his narration from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, that he said concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ﴾ — he said: the people of falsehood; ﴿إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ رَبُّكَ﴾ — he said: the people of truth; ﴿وَلِذٰلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ﴾ — he said: for mercy He created the people of Paradise.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear, explanatory statement.
And whoever also said "He created them for disagreement" does not contradict this, because he holds that the meaning is: and He created the people of falsehood for disagreement.
The clearest of them is the view of al-Ḥasan which we mentioned, and the meaning would be: the people of falsehood will not cease to disagree about their religion, except those on whom Allah has mercy — and the people of Islam do not disagree about their religion — and for that He created the people of felicity for felicity and the people of wretchedness for wretchedness. This is made clear by His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
It is also said: The implied form (taqdīr) is: they forbid corruption in the land, and for that He created them.

nahhas-meani:120-120.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكُـلاًّ نَّقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ ٱلرُّسُلِ مَا نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤَادَكَ﴾.
That is, We increase you in steadfastness by it, as He said, exalted be His mention: ﴿قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ؟ قَالَ بَلَى وَلَكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَآءَكَ فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَمَوْعِظَةٌ وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
Abū Mūsā, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid said: ﴿فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾: in this sūra. [Translator's note: the source places the colon after «قال أبو موسى», as if Abū Mūsā were reporting from the others; translated as a joint attribution.]
Shuʿba said: I heard Qatāda say: in this world.
This view is good, except that it is objected to on the ground that it would be said — the truth has come to him in this sūra and in others — though this is not binding, because it does not negate anything [else]. Do you not see that it is said "So-and-so is in the truth" when death comes to him, without meaning by it that he had been in falsehood? So this sūra would have been singled out for this by way of emphasis, because of the narratives and admonitions in it.

nahhas-meani:121-121.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُل لِّلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ ٱعْمَلُواْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنَّا عَامِلُونَ﴾.
That is, [we are] acting [with respect to] what you are upon.
This is a threat and a warning. Do you not see that after it comes ﴿وَانْتَظِرُوا إنَّا مُنْتَظِرُونَ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾?!

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, marked.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says سَوَّمتُ الشيء when you mark it. And it is narrated that there were things like signet rings upon them.
Al-Ḥasan said: Marked; and in this there is evidence that they were not stones of this world, and that they were among what [they] were punished with.
And one says سوَّمت الشيءَ when you send it forth freely; except that this has not been said about this word.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا هِيَ مِنَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: By this He strikes fear into Quraysh.
Someone else said: The meaning is: from the wrongdoers of this community.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The two views come back to a single meaning.
It is also said: And it is not far from whoever does the deed of the people of Lot.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِلَىٰ مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْباً﴾.
The meaning: and to the people of Midian.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَنقُصُواْ ٱلْمِكْيَالَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ إِنِّيۤ أَرَاكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: Their prices were cheap.
What the language points to is that it is general.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَقِيَّةُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: Your share from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Mujāhid said: That is, obedience to Allah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning is: that whose reward remains for him.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰشُعَيْبُ أَصَلَٰوتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَن نَّتْرُكَ مَا يَعْبُدُ ءابَاؤُنَآ﴾.
Sufyān said, from al-Aʿmash: That is, your recitation.
And He indicated by this that they were disbelievers.
Then He said: ﴿أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِيۤ أَمْوَالِنَا مَا نَشَاءُ﴾?
It is narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam that he said: Among what he forbade them was clipping dirhams.
It is also said: The meaning of ﴿أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِيۤ أَمْوَالِنَا مَا نَشَاءُ﴾ is: when we agree among ourselves to short-measuring, why do you forbid us from it?
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning of ﴿إِنَّكَ لأَنتَ ٱلْحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ﴾ is by way of mockery.
Someone else said: Its meaning is: you are indeed the forbearing, the right-minded — in your own estimation.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ يٰقَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّي وَرَزَقَنِي مِنْهُ رِزْقاً حَسَناً﴾.
It is said: lawful [provision].
It is also said: the obedience he was enabled to perform.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, I do not forbid you something and then commit it myself.
And the meaning of ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ﴾ is: and to Him I return.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيٰقَوْمِ لاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شِقَاقِيۤ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, let it not drive you.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-shiqāq in the language is enmity, as though he comes to be on a side (shiqq) other than the other's side.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا قَوْمُ لُوطٍ مِّنكُم بِبَعِيدٍ﴾.
It is said: The nearest of the destructions they knew of was the destruction of the people of Lot.
That is: so the admonition for you in it is clear, because of its nearness to you.

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰشُعَيْبُ مَا نَفْقَهُ كَثِيراً مِّمَّا تَقُولُ وَإِنَّا لَنَرَاكَ فِينَا ضَعِيفاً﴾.
Sufyān said: It has reached us that he was afflicted in his sight.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The lexicographers have reported that Ḥimyar call a blind man ḍaʿīf (weak), i.e. he has become weak through the loss of his sight; just as he is called ḍarīr, i.e. he has been harmed through the loss of his sight; and just as he is called makfūf, i.e. he has been withheld from seeing through the loss of his sight.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ رَهْطُكَ لَرَجَمْنَاكَ﴾.
That is, were it not for your clan, we would have killed you by stoning. ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَرَهْطِي أعَزُّ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ اللهِ﴾, i.e. you claim that you refrain from killing me for the sake of my clan, yet you do not fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in rejecting His command?!
And it is said: His clan were of their religion, and for that reason they showed inclination towards them.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وَرَآءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيّاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, you have abandoned what I brought you.
The lexicographers said: The meaning is: and you have taken the command of Allah behind you, cast behind your backs (ẓihriyyan). One says اتَّخذتُه ظِهْرياً and جعلتُ حاجَته بِظَهْرٍ (I put his need behind my back), i.e. when you do not attend to it.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَخَذَتِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ الصَّيْحَةُ﴾.
It is narrated that Gabriel ﷺ gave a shout at them and they all died. This is made clear by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَأَصْبَحُواْ فِي دِيَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ﴾, i.e. dead, without any movement.

nahhas-meani:95-95.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْاْ فِيهَآ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, as though they had never lived there.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned it earlier, and it is taken from sound (al-ṣawt), because a dwelling is only called maghnan when its people are in it.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلاَ بُعْداً لِّمَدْيَنَ كَمَا بَعِدَتْ ثَمُودُ﴾.
One says بَعِدَ يَبْعَدُ when someone perishes; and from distance [in place], بَعُدَ يبعُدُ.

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِآيَاتِنَا وَسُلْطَانٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
Al-sulṭān is the proof; and from this the governor is called sulṭān, because he is the proof of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, on earth.
And it is said: It is taken from al-salīṭ, which is that with which light is made [i.e. lamp oil].

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ بِئْسَ ٱلرِّفْدُ ٱلْمَرْفُودُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They were given an additional curse on the Day of Resurrection.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-rifd in the language is help and giving; and the meaning that stands for them in place of help is the curse.
The implied form (taqdīr): "Evil is the gift, the gift of the one given (rifd al-marfūd)."

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤر كِتَابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ﴾.
The meaning is: It is a Book whose verses have been made firm [Translator's note: كِتَابٌ being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ].
Al-Ḥasan said: They were made firm with command and prohibition, then expounded with reward and punishment.
Qatāda said: By Allah, He made them firm against falsehood, then expounded them with His knowledge, and made clear their lawful and their unlawful, obedience and disobedience.
Mujāhid said: «فُصِّلت» means: explained.
And it was said: They were made firm, so nothing after them abrogates them; then «فُصِّلت»: they were sent down one thing after another.
And among the best of them is Qatāda's view: that is, He made them firm against defect and falsehood.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مِن لَّدُنْ حَكِيمٍ خَبِيرٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, from One All-Wise, All-Aware.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَلاَّ تَعْبُدُوۤاْ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهَ إِنَّنِي لَكُمْ مِّنْهُ نَذِيرٌ وَبَشِيرٌ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: [expounded] with [the message] that you should worship none but Allah.
And it is possible that the meaning is: so that you should not worship [anyone else].
And it is possible that the meaning is: you have been commanded to worship none but Allah.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنِ ٱسْتَغْفِرُواْ رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوۤاْ إِلَيْهِ يُمَتِّعْكُمْ مَّتَاعاً حَسَناً إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾.
«يُمَتِّعكم»: He will give you long life; and it was said: He will not destroy you.
The origin of «الإمتاع» is prolonging; and from it is «أمْتَعَ اللهُ بك» and «متَّع» (may Allah let [others] enjoy you long).
Qatāda said: "to an appointed term", that is, until death.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُؤْتِ كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ﴾.
That is: whoever has a righteous deed will be given its reward.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ لِيَسْتَخْفُواْ مِنْهُ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād said: One of them would pass by the Prophet ﷺ and bend his chest and cover himself with his garment, disliking that the Prophet ﷺ should see him.
Abū Razīn said: A man would lie down on his side and cover himself with his garment in order to hide.
Mujāhid said: ﴿يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ﴾ out of doubt and wavering, ﴿لِيَسْتَخْفُواْ مِنْهُ﴾, that is, from Allah, if they could.
Al-Ḥasan said: He means the talk of the soul. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that when they cover themselves with their garments in the darkness of the night and in the recesses of their houses, He knows at that very hour what they conceal and what they make public.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These meanings are close to one another, that is, they conceal enmity towards the Prophet ﷺ and fold [it within].
And among the sound reports about it is what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us; he said: al-Zaʿfarānī said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us; he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād ibn Jaʿfar informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās reading: ﴿أَلاَ إنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْني صُدُورُهُمْ﴾. He said: I asked him about it, and he said: "Some people were too shy to relieve themselves [in the open] and so be exposed to the sky, and this was revealed concerning them."
And it is narrated that one of them said: I have locked my door, let down my curtain, covered myself with my garment and bent my chest — so who knows about me? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He knows what they conceal and what they make public.
Its parallel is ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوَى ثَلاَثَةٍ إلاَّ هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾.
Whoever reads ﴿تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ﴾ — and it is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās — takes it in the sense of intensification, as it is said «احْلَوْلَى الشيءُ» (the thing became very sweet). And [their chests] do not «تَثْنَوْنِي» unless they bend them, so the meaning comes back to that.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا﴾.
Of everything that creeps, of people and others, it is said «دابّ» and «دابّة», [the latter] by way of intensification — a feminine [form] according to attribute and natural make-up.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: ﴿مُسْتقرُّها﴾ is in the womb, and ﴿مستودَعُها﴾ is in the ground in which it dies.
Miqsam said, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās: Its dwelling-place is where it takes shelter, and its depository is where it dies in the earth.
And it was said: ﴿مُسْتَقَرُّهَا﴾ is that upon which its deeds settle, and ﴿مستودعها﴾ is what it comes to.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: Its dwelling-place is in the womb, and its depository is in the loins.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَق ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾.
So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed that whoever is able to do this, nothing is beyond His power.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَكَانَ عَرْشُهُ عَلَى ٱلْمَآءِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās: Upon what was the water, when He had not yet created a heaven or an earth? He said: Upon the back of the wind.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلاً﴾.
That is: to test you, so that there would appear from you that for which He will requite you, because He only requites for the deed, even though He knew it before.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِن قُلْتَ إِنَّكُمْ مَّبْعُوثُونَ مِن بَعْدِ ٱلْمَوْتِ لَيَقُولَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
And it is read ﴿سَاحِرٌ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: Magic for them is falsehood, so it is as though they said: This is nothing but falsehood.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَخَّرْنَا عَنْهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابَ إِلَىٰ أُمَّةٍ مَّعْدُودَةٍ﴾.
[Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, until a counted term.]
Mujāhid said: That is, until a time.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ﴾
That is: the recompense of their mockery. And the meaning is: the punishment encompassed them.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا ٱلإِنْسَانَ﴾.
That is: the disbelievers. ﴿مِنَّا رَحْمَةً﴾: that is, provision.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ﴾.
An exception not from the first [category] (munqaṭiʿ), in the sense of «لكنْ» (but). And it is possible that it is an exception from the hāʾ (pronoun), because its implied construction is «إنّ الإنسانَ», and "man" is the genus.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن يَقُولُواْ لَوْلاَ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنزٌ أَوْ جَآءَ مَعَهُ مَلَكٌ﴾.
That is: out of dislike that they should say [Translator's note: an omitted muḍāf, «كراهةَ», as object of purpose].
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ نَذِيرٌ﴾, that is: your duty is only to warn them; it is not your duty to bring them the signs they have proposed.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُواْ بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِّثْلِهِ﴾.
The meaning is: each sūra of them like a sūra of it. ﴿وَٱدْعُواْ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: that is, to help you.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا وَهُمْ فِيهَا لاَ يُبْخَسُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means the idolaters: when they do a deed they are requited for it in this world.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Whoever does a deed intending by it other than Allah is requited for it in this world.
Mujāhid said: Whoever does a deed and it is not accepted from him is given its reward in this world.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The best of them is al-Ḍaḥḥāk's view, because of His saying after that: ﴿أُوْلَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ فِى الآخِرَةِ إلاَّ النَّارُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿لاَ يُبْخَسُونَ﴾: they will not be shortchanged.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾.
ʿIkrima, Ibrāhīm and Manṣūr said: He means the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿وَيَتْلُوهُ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْهُ﴾: Gabriel, peace be upon him.
Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm said: ﴿شَاهِدٌ مِّنْهُ﴾, that is, Gabriel ﷺ.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿شَاهِدٌ مِّنْهُ﴾ means his tongue.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾ is Muḥammad ﷺ; ﴿وَيَتْلُوهُ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْهُ﴾, that is, from Allah, and it is Gabriel, peace be upon him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Saʿīd ibn Mūsā narrated to me in Qarqīsiyā; he said: Makhlad ibn Mālik narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Salama, from Khuṣayf: ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾ — he said: the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَيَتْلُوهُ شَاهِدٌ مِّنْهُ﴾ — he said: Gabriel, peace be upon him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The hāʾ (pronoun) in ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ would be for the Prophet ﷺ; in ﴿يَتْلُوهُ﴾ it refers back to «البيّنة» (the clear proof) [hence masculine], because «البيّنة» and «البيان» are one; and in ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ it refers back to the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And al-Ḥasan's view admits the meaning: and his tongue expresses it and makes it distinct.
And it is possible that the hāʾ in ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ refers back to ﴿مَنْ﴾.
And it was said: The witness is the Qurʾān; ﴿وَيَتْلُوهُ﴾: it comes after it, following as a witness; ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ﴾: that is, and before the witness. And it has been said that by ﴿أَفَمَن كَانَ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾ the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims are meant, and the holder of this view cited as evidence His saying ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾. The meaning on the first view is: Is one who stands on clear proof from his Lord like one who desires the life of this world and its adornment? [Translator's note: the khabar being omitted].
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَىٰ إَمَاماً وَرَحْمَةً﴾.
That is: it confirms it.
And it was said: It is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الشاهد», that is: and the Book of Moses follows it.
Mujāhid said concerning His saying ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَىٰ﴾: the Torah.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِهِ مِنَ ٱلأَحْزَابِ فَٱلنَّارُ مَوْعِدُهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: «الأحزاب» are the people of all the religions.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Whenever I found a ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ to be authentic, I would find its confirmation in the Book of Allah. So I reflected on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "No one hears of me and then does not believe in me — neither Jew nor Christian — except that he enters the Fire." So I sought its confirmation in the Book of Allah, and there it was: ﴿وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِهِ مِنَ ٱلأَحْزَابِ فَٱلنَّارُ مَوْعِدُهُ﴾. And «الأحزاب» (the factions) are the people of all the religions, because they wage war on one another.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً أُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ وَيَقُولُ ٱلأَشْهَادُ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَبُواْ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «الأشهاد» are the prophets and the messengers. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذَا جِئْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ وَجِئْنَا بِكَ عَلَى هَؤُلاَءِ شَهِيداً﴾.
Mujāhid said: «الأشهاد» are the angels.
Sufyān said: I asked al-Aʿmash about «الأشهاد», and he said: They are the angels.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُضَاعَفُ لَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ مَا كَانُواْ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَمَا كَانُواْ يُبْصِرُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: They were not able to hear a report [of truth] and benefit from it, nor did they see good and take hold of it.
Al-Farrāʾ reported from some of the exegetes that the meaning is: the punishment will be doubled for them because they were able to hear and yet did not understand.
And he held that this is like their saying: «جزيته فعلَه» and «بفعلِه» (I requited him his deed / for his deed) [Translator's note: i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition].
And among the best of what has been said about it — and it is the sense of Ibn ʿAbbās's view — is that the meaning is: they were not able to hear the truth with the hearing of one who benefits, nor to see it with the sight of one who is guided, because of their preoccupation with the disbelief in which they persisted.
And it is narrated from him: ﴿مَا كَانُواْ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ٱلسَّمْعَ﴾ — he means the gods [they worshipped].

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ كَٱلأَعْمَىٰ وَٱلأَصَمِّ وَٱلْبَصِيرِ وَٱلسَّمِيعِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The blind and the deaf are a likeness for the disbeliever, and the seeing and the hearing are a likeness for the believer.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, indicated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلاً﴾? This indicates that this is for two [parties].

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قِوْمِهِ مَا نَرَاكَ إِلاَّ بَشَراً مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَاكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا﴾.
«الملأ» are the chiefs, and «الأراذل» are the wicked who are not chiefs; their singular is «أرذل».
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأْيِ﴾.
And it is read ﴿بَادئ الرَّأى﴾ with hamza. The meaning of the form with hamza is "at the outset of opinion", that is: they followed you only without reflecting or considering; had they reflected, they would not have followed you.
And the meaning of the form without hamza is: they followed you in outward opinion, while inwardly they are otherwise.
It is said: «بَدَا يَبْدُو» when something becomes apparent.
And it is possible that its meaning is: they followed you in outward opinion and did not reflect on its inner reality and its outcome; so on this view it would have the meaning of the form with hamza.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ يٰقَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّيۤ﴾.
That is: upon certainty and clarity. This is a reply to them, because they found fault with those who followed him, so he said: ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّيۤ﴾, that is: if I am upon clear proof from my Lord, then whoever follows me is clear-sighted and forgiven.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَآتَانِي رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِهِ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: He means the message (al-risāla), because it is a blessing and a mercy.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَعَمِيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
That is: you did not understand it. It is said: «عَمِيتُ عن كذا» and «عَمِيَ عليَّ كذا», that is, I did not understand it. And the meaning is: so the mercy was obscured.
And it is read ﴿فَعُمِّيَتْ﴾, and it was said: it is like «دَخَلَ الخفُّ في رجلي» (the boot went into my foot) — a figurative usage [with inversion], except that the mercy is what is obscured, and the one who has it is the one who is blind [to it].
Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿وَآتَانِي رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِهِ﴾: Islam and guidance, wisdom and prophethood.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوهَا وَأَنتُمْ لَهَا كَارِهُونَ﴾.
That is: Shall we make it binding upon you while you are averse to understanding it?

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَآ أَنَاْ بِطَارِدِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾.
By this He indicated that they had asked him to drive them away.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ مُّلاَقُو رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
That is: and He will requite whoever drives them away for what he did.
Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning of ﴿مَنْ يَنْصُرُنِي﴾ is: who will protect me?

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ أَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزْدَرِيۤ أَعْيُنُكُمْ﴾.
The meaning of «تَزْدَرِي» is: you think little of them and hold them in contempt. It is said: «زريتُ على الرجلِ» when you found fault with him and held his deed in contempt, and «أزريتُ به» when you belittled him.
And the meaning is: You said that these followed me in outward opinion; but I only call to the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, so whoever follows me I accept, and what is hidden is not my responsibility.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰنُوحُ قَدْ جَادَلْتَنَا فَأَكْثَرْتَ جِدَالَنَا فَأْتَنِا بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read: ﴿فَأَكْثَرْتَ جَدَلَنَا﴾. «الجِدال» and «الجَدَل» are going to extremes in disputation.
Mujāhid said: ﴿جَادَلْتَنَا﴾, that is, you have argued with us.
Al-Zajjāj said: And the meaning of ﴿إنْ كَانَ اللهُ يُرِيدُ أنْ يُغْوِيَكُمْ﴾ is: to lead you astray and destroy you.
And it was said: to disappoint you.
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] said: ﴿يُغْوِيَكُمْ﴾: to destroy you with His punishment. He reported from [the tribe of] Ṭayyiʾ: «أصبَحَ فلانٌ غاوياً», that is, sick; and «أغويته»: I destroyed him; and from this is ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا﴾.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَاهُ قُلْ إِنِ ٱفْتَرَيْتُهُ فَعَلَيَّ إِجْرَامِي﴾.
That is: if I fabricated it, then upon me is the sin of fabrication. ﴿وَأَنَاْ بَرِيۤءٌ مِّمَّا تُجْرَمُونَ﴾: that is, of your denial.
And whoever read (أَجْرَامِي) with fatḥa on the hamza took it as the plural of «جُرْم» (crime).

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأُوحِيَ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ أَنَّهُ لَن يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إِلاَّ مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: So he supplicated against them; that is, when he was informed of this, he said: ﴿إنَّكَ إنْ تَذَرْهُمْ يُضلُّوا عِبَادَكَ وَلاَ يَلِدُوا إلاَّ فَاجِراً كَفَّاراً﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: That is, so do not grieve.
Abū Jaʿfar said: According to the people of language it is grief accompanied by abjectness.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَصْنَعُ ٱلْفُلْكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلأٌ مِّن قَوْمِهِ سَخِرُواْ مِنْهُ﴾.
It is narrated that they used to pass by him while he was building the ship and say: This one who used to claim that he was a prophet has become a carpenter.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَالَ إِن تَسْخَرُواْ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسْخَرُ مِنكُمْ كَمَا تَسْخَرُونَ﴾.
That is: if you regard us as ignorant, we regard you as ignorant, just as you regarded us as ignorant.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن يَأْتِيهِ عَذَابٌ يُخْزِيهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذَابٌ مُّقِيمٌ﴾.
That is: whoever's affair ends up in this — he is the ignorant one.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ﴾.
It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: That is, and the dawn broke — as though he took it to refer to the brightening (tanwīr) of the morning.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: «التنّور» is the face of the earth, and it was a sign between Noah and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He; that is: when you see the water gushing over the face of the earth, then board the ship, you and your companions.
Qatāda said: «التنّور» is the highest and most elevated part of the earth, and that was a sign for him.
Mujāhid used to hold that it was the baker's oven.
Al-Shaʿbī said: The water came from the direction of Kufa.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are not contradictory, because Allah has informed us that the water came from the sky and the earth, saying: ﴿فَفَتَحْنَا أبْوَابَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَاءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ. وَفَجَّرْنَا الأرْضَ عُيُوناً﴾; so these views meet in that it was a sign.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱحْمِلْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, male and female.
Qatāda said: That is, of every two kinds.
«الزوج» in the language is one that has another with it which it cannot do without.
It is said: «عندي زوجان من الخِفاف» (I have a pair of boots), and the like.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَهْلَكَ إِلاَّ مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾.
That is: except the one against whom the word of destruction has gone forth.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَنْ آمَنَ﴾, that is, and carry whoever has believed.
Then His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: He carried eighty with him.
Qatāda said: Only eight believed with him: five sons and three women. «[Translator's note: «خمسة بنين» (five sons) is as printed; the commonly reported figure is Noah, his wife, three sons and their three wives.]»

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱرْكَبُواْ فِيهَا بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ مَجْريٰهَا
 وَمُرْسَاهَا﴾.
That is: by Allah is its being made to sail and its being made to anchor.
And whoever read ﴿مَجْرَاهَا ومَرْسَاهَا﴾ took the meaning to be: its sailing and its anchoring, that is, its coming to rest. «[Translator's note: the source prints both readings with the same consonantal form; the first discussed is presumably «مُجْراها ومُرْساها» (verbal nouns of Form IV), the second «مَجْراها ومَرْساها» (verbal nouns of Form I).]»
It is narrated from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī that he read ﴿باسْمِ اللهِ مُجْرِيهَا وَمُرْسِيهَا﴾ as an adjective (naʿt) [of Allah].

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُ وَكَانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: The wife of a prophet never committed adultery; and he was his son.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He was his son, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed us of that.
ʿIkrima said: If you wish, I will swear to you that he was his son.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He was his son; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He was not his son, and what makes that clear is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿فَلاَ تَسْأَلْنِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: He was not his son; he was only born on his bed, so he was ascribed to him.
The first view is clearer and sounder, because of the eminence of those who held it, and because His saying ﴿إنَّه لَيْسَ مِنْ أهْلِكَ﴾ is not something that negates his being his son. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Its meaning is: he is not of the people of your religion, nor of the people of your allegiance.
Sufyān said: Its meaning is: he is not of your family whom I promised you I would save.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These two views are good linguistically, and the first is more fitting.
Abū Muʿāwiya narrated from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that he read ﴿وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُ وَكَانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ﴾, meaning «ابنَها» (her son), then he dropped the alif. «[Translator's note: the source prints the standard text here; the reading meant is «ابْنَهَ» (with fatḥa on the hāʾ, standing for ابنها).]»
Something like this is not permissible according to the scholars of Arabic, as far as I know.
And it is possible that the meaning of ﴿وَكَانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ﴾ is: apart from his father's religion; or it may be apart from the ship — and this is more likely.
And the meaning of ﴿يَعْصِمُنِي﴾ is: protects me.
